summary: Precedents found for an iOS/macOS port of a MuJoCo-plus-learning project. (1) MuJoCo itself: the official C library and Python wheels run on macOS Apple Silicon (PyPI 3.17.0 ships macosx_11_0_arm64 wheels; no iOS wheel exists); the official docs list only Windows, Linux and macOS. iOS has two precedents: the shipping App Store app iMuJoCo (MuJoCo physics on iPhone/iPad with Swift UI and Metal rendering, UDP state streaming, iOS 26.0+, promised Apache 2.0 source not yet published) and liuliu/swift-mujoco (Swift Package, "should work on macOS, Linux and iOS", GL context only on macOS/Linux, pinned at MuJoCo 2.3.0). (2) GPU physics on Apple: MJX-JAX officially lists Apple Silicon, but Apple's jax-metal is "experimental", its last release was over a year old as of Jan 2026, and forum users report it broken for MJX as of Sep 2025 and Apr 2026; MJX-Warp targets NVIDIA only; a third-party MJX-MLX port exists with 26.7 steps/sec on simple scenes and only cartpole/pendulum validation. (3) On-device training on iPhone: Apple Core ML MLUpdateTask (iOS 13+, updates a compiled updatable model from labeled batches, classifier sample); MLX Swift MNISTTrainer (trains a LeNet on iOS and macOS, Xcode-only Metal shader build); ExecuTorch training is "experimental", backward graph captured ahead of time, loss embedded in the model, backend integration "work in progress", validated only on Android in its paper. (4) macOS Apple-Silicon training throughput: MuJoCo docs measure CPU MuJoCo at 650K single-humanoid steps/sec on an M3 Max versus 950K for MJX-JAX on an A100 (batch 8192) and 1.8M on a 64-core AMD CPU; the arXiv paper 2501.14925 finds "a significant performance gap between Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs" for LLM training; Stable-Baselines3's MPS issue reports CPU faster than MPS for RL and SB3 "not compatible with MPS" (2022, maintainers later pointed to SBX/JAX); PyTorch MPS backend is "in the beta phase" and supports custom Metal kernels, but no tutorial exists for porting custom CUDA kernels. (5) Rendering: iMuJoCo uses Metal; Apple's RealityRenderer bridges RealityKit scenes into a Metal workflow; no open-source RealityKit/SceneKit MuJoCo visualizer was found. (6) Other engines: PhysX 5.1 got an ios64 build preset via a community PR (closed unmerged, maintained in the O3DE fork; CUDA-only systems unsupported on iOS); Bullet re-hosts to iOS as plain C++. Code-side facts: UEMA_Research pins torch 2.6.0+cu124 and mujoco 3.3.0, hard-codes cuda:0 as capture and training device, calls torch.cuda.current_stream().synchronize() in the training step, builds a pure-C++ (no CUDA kernels) load_inline extension that auto-detects MSVC, and documents that the D3D12/CUDA vision transport is Windows/Unreal-only and excluded; no "mps" device string appears anywhere in Source.

open_questions: iMuJoCo's promised Apache 2.0 source has no public repository found; whether it exposes a reusable Metal renderer for MuJoCo scenes is unknown until it is published.

Whether the full MuJoCo 3.x C library cross-compiles for iOS (arm64, no AVX) with its contact solver intact is undocumented; swift-mujoco claims iOS at MuJoCo 2.3.0 only, and the official docs say the library 'requires a processor with AVX instructions'.

No measured report was found of a MuJoCo RL agent training on an M-series Mac with the same job timed on an NVIDIA card; the only like-for-like numbers are MuJoCo's own CPU-physics figures (M3 Max 650K steps/s vs A100 MJX-JAX 950K steps/s) and the LLM-training gap paper.

Whether the project's eight-world process-separated replay training (README line 72 names it as excluded from the release) and the GLFW-based mujoco.Renderer can run under macOS without the Windows shared-memory frame transport was not tested.

ExecuTorch training on an Apple delegate (CoreML or MPS) has no published example; its README says backend integration is a work in progress, so an iPhone training path for a PyTorch-defined model is unproven.

Core ML's MLUpdateTask documentation seen here covers only classifier personalization; which layer types are updatable (needed to judge whether a transformer forward model could be updated on-phone) was not readable from the fetched pages.
The MJX-MLX port's 26.7 steps/sec figure has no scene description or hardware named beside it, so it cannot be placed against the 650K steps/sec CPU figure.
The Towards AI article cited by search for an M3 Max throughput number returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

summary: iOS: Python 3.13+ runs on iOS only as an embedded interpreter (CPython tier 3, PEP 730; Python-Apple-support supplies the Python.xcframework; Pyto is a shipped App Store app built this way, and App Store guideline 2.5.2 allows self-contained bundles). The release's training path cannot run on an iPhone as written: PoolSource spawns one process per body (multiprocessing "spawn", datasource.py line 495) and the Python docs state an iOS app cannot use any form of subprocessing or multiprocessing; the pinned torch==2.6.0 has no iOS wheel (macOS arm64 wheels only), and the BeeWare iOS wheel index holds numpy, pillow and matplotlib but not scipy, torch, opencv, mujoco, scikit-learn, pyyaml, psutil, imageio, trimesh, safetensors, gymnasium or networkx; MIMo's vision.py imports cv2 at module level; MuJoCo's classic renderer needs OpenGL 1.5 and Apple lists OpenGL ES on iOS as available only through iOS 12.0, so eye rendering (env.py EyeRenderer, mujoco.GLContext) needs a Metal path (the iMuJoCo App Store app shows MuJoCo physics plus Metal rendering is buildable on iOS 26). Per-app memory on an 8 GB iPhone is not documented by Apple; one developer measured a ~6144 MB process budget on an iPhone 16 Pro Max with the increased-memory-limit entitlement, and Apple's os_proc_available_memory doc says limits change during the app life cycle. Background execution: five seconds after entering background, extendable by beginBackgroundTask, then termination; BGProcessingTask runs minutes only while the device is idle. Thermal: Apple says reduce system resource use at higher thermal states. iOS file access is limited to the app sandbox. macOS by contrast: aarch64-apple-darwin is CPython tier 1; mujoco 3.3.0 and torch 2.6.0 both publish macosx_11_0_arm64 wheels for cp313; the code already selects CPU when CUDA is absent (lem_model.py line 785) and disables autocast off CUDA (line 800); torch's MPS backend exists but has no float64 (the code holds 86 float64 references, 5 in torch tensors) and the autocast call is hard-coded to "cuda" (line 2665); the native C++ helper compiles with an MSVC-only setup and falls back to pure Python; the NVRTC patchify kernel loads only when CUDA is available. Measured Windows resume used 4,287 MB of GPU memory and ~30 GB committed memory for trainer plus eight world processes, which exceeds any reported iPhone per-app budget. Feasible on macOS (CPU, or MPS with float64 and autocast changes); feasible on iOS only as a single-process inference/viewer app with rebuilt binary dependencies, not as the training run.

summary: What is documented: MuJoCo's maintainers state support for Windows, Linux and macOS only (prebuilt libraries for x86_64 and arm64; macOS universal), and no official statement, build target, release asset or issue names iOS or iPadOS. The core engine is plain C with a CMake 3.16 / C++17 build that has an Emscripten (WebAssembly) branch, so the physics library is already compiled for a non-desktop target without OpenGL; nothing in the CMake files references iOS. The classic renderer (mjr_ functions, mjrContext) is written against desktop OpenGL 1.5 fixed-function calls through a bundled glad loader (glMatrixMode, glColor4f, glEnable in render_gl2.c), and the Python bindings' GL context has exactly three platform branches (Linux glx/egl/osmesa, Windows wgl, Darwin cgl) with no iOS branch; iOS provides only OpenGL ES, which Apple deprecated in iOS 12 (secondhand quote of Apple's notes). MuJoCo's newer Filament renderer declares a graphics-API enum with OPENGL ("desktop, mobile (GLES), web (WebGL)") and VULKAN, and no Metal value, even though the Filament engine itself supports Metal on iOS and macOS. What is reported by individual users: (1) liuliu/swift-mujoco (third-party, listed in MuJoCo's README) says it "should work on macOS, Linux and iOS" with GLContext only on macOS and Linux, pinned to a 2022-era MuJoCo 2.3 fork, last release "3 years ago"; (2) the radcli14/swift-mujoco fork says it vendors MuJoCo 3.9.0 and builds headless (physics, compiler and editing API only, no renderer, UI or simulate) for macOS, iOS device + simulator and visionOS, with mjUSEPLATFORMSIMD deliberately undefined because it pulls x86 AVX; (3) iMuJoCo, a free App Store app by XIAOCHEN WANG first released Mar 2, 2026, claims MuJoCo on iPhone/iPad "with native Swift UI and Metal rendering", requires iOS 26.0, has under 1k downloads and a stated but not yet delivered Apache 2.0 open-source plan; (4) mujoco-mac-metal is an experimental Metal stepping package for macOS Apple Silicon only, with rendering still through MuJoCo's OpenGL; (5) MuJoCo AR and mujoco-ar-viewer only stream poses or scenes to a phone or Vision Pro, they do not run MuJoCo on the device. So an iPhone app would use the headless C library plus its own Metal (or SceneKit/RealityKit) renderer fed from mjvScene geometry, which is what iMuJoCo reports doing; no Swift or Objective-C bindings are first-party. App Store rules: Guideline 2.5.2 forbids downloading or executing code that changes the app's features and requires apps to stay inside their container; DPLA 3.3.1(B) allows downloaded interpreted code only under three conditions. A MuJoCo model XML is a data file parsed by the bundled engine, not executable code, and neither Apple text names simulators or model files, so permissibility of run-time XML loading is an inference, not a documented ruling. On the UEMA_Research side: requirements.txt pins mujoco==3.3.0 and torch 2.6.0 from the CUDA 12.4 index, the README requires an NVIDIA card, the vision path renders through mujoco.GLContext plus mjr_ offscreen buffers (env.py), the model falls back to CPU when CUDA is absent (lem_model.py line 785), and the two JIT C++ extensions (native_ops.py includes cuda.h; vision_kernels.py is CUDA) both document pure-Python fallbacks. PyTorch's MPS device documents GPU training on macOS 15+ with no float64; ExecuTorch's on-device training is described by its own README as an experimental technical preview, so an iPhone training path is not documented.

summary: MuJoCo on macOS Apple Silicon in 2026: the physics engine is CPU C code shipped as native arm64 wheels (3.17.0, Oct 22, 2026: cp310-cp315 macosx_11_0_arm64 only; the pinned 3.3.0 also has a cp313 arm64 wheel) and as a universal2 DMG holding MuJoCo.app (simulate) and mujoco.framework for Xcode. Headless offscreen rendering works on macOS through the Apple CGL backend, which the Python bindings pick by default on Darwin (MUJOCO_GL valid values on macOS: cgl, glfw, on/off forms; egl/osmesa are Linux-only), and since 2.3.4 it is not restricted to the main thread; a context may be current on one thread at a time. The GLFW backend creates an invisible window and the interactive viewer needs mjpython (main-thread rule); an open Sept 2026 issue shows NSWindow-off-main-thread failures for the native viewer. UEMA_Research's env.py already uses mujoco.GLContext directly (one context per spawned worker process), which maps onto CGL on macOS without change; only phase0/run_benchmark.py forces MUJOCO_GL=glfw. MJX-JAX lists Apple Silicon as supported, but JAX's own docs say Mac GPU is not supported/experimental, Apple's jax-metal is experimental with no float64, and user reports show MJX failing on Metal with "failed to legalize operation 'mhlo.reduce'" and falling back to the JAX CPU backend; UEMA_Research does not use MJX. The project's GPU dependence is in PyTorch, not MuJoCo: requirements pin torch==2.6.0+cu124, the README requires an NVIDIA card, 168 torch.cuda references in 38 files, 163 literal "cuda" device strings, a C++ extension built with_cuda=True linking cuda.lib and MSVC detection, and nvcc vision kernels; both native parts fall back to Python paths, and lem_model.py falls to CPU (never MPS) when CUDA is absent. torch 2.6.0 has macOS arm64 wheels (CPU+MPS); MPS lacks float64, which attention_cap.py uses. iOS: MuJoCo's CMakeLists has macOS framework options but no iOS lines; a third-party Swift binding claims iOS without GLContext; Python on iOS is embedded-only and cannot use subprocessing or multiprocessing, which the trainer's PoolSource (spawned worker processes) depends on. No official MuJoCo physics benchmark on Apple Silicon was found.

summary: Research on running and training the UEMA_Research code on Apple hardware, with every claim tied to a file line or a fetched page. The release's trainer is hard-wired to CUDA: `lem_model.py:785` collapses any non-CUDA device to "cpu", `lem_model.py:798-800` turns mixed precision off except on CUDA, `lem_model.py:2665` names "cuda" in `torch.amp.autocast`, `lem_model.py:1876` uses the fused AdamW only on CUDA, and the optional C++ extension (`lem/native_ops.py:3219-3225`) is built with `with_cuda=True` and `cuda.lib` but falls back to pure Python when it fails to compile (`native_ops.py:11`, `training_step.py:22-27`, `replay_buffer.py:282-285`). Two float64-on-device sites (`lem_model.py:2533-2534`, `hand_response.py:107`) would raise on MPS, since MPS has no float64 (library error text documented on the PyTorch forum). PyTorch on macOS: arm64 wheels exist for 2.6.0 through 2.9.0 (PyPI); MPS autocast accepts bfloat16 and float16 only (v2.9.0 `torch/amp/autocast_mode.py`; bfloat16 autocast added in 2.6.0, released 29 Jan 2025); GradScaler on MPS failed in 2.6.0 (`.double()` in `unscale_`) and gained an mps branch by 2.8.0; `torch.compile` for Metal is a 2.7.0 prototype and `MPSInductor` a 2.8.0 feature; 2.9.0 requires macOS 14; unsupported ops raise unless `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1` routes them to the CPU; the MPS allocator caps memory at 1.7 x recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize (itself about 75% of system memory), adjustable with `PYTORCH_MPS_HIGH_WATERMARK_RATIO` or `torch.mps.set_per_process_memory_fraction`; MPS tensors through DataLoader workers needed the fork start method (issue 87688) and a Python 3.12+ macOS queue hang is open (issue 153050). PyTorch on iOS: PyTorch Mobile "is no longer actively supported"; ExecuTorch has an experimental training extension (SGD and AdamW, Adam "planned", backward graph captured ahead of time, loss embedded in the model, "Integration with backends/delegates is still a work in progress"), its iOS package needs iOS 17 / macOS 14 and ships Core ML, MLX (experimental) and XNNPACK frameworks, and its MPS backend is deprecated as of ExecuTorch 1.2 for removal in 1.4. Apple MLX: Python, C++, C and Swift APIs; needs Apple silicon, macOS >= 14, Python >= 3.10; Adam/AdamW optimizers; `mx.load` reads `.safetensors` (the release checkpoint is `model.safetensors`); mlx-swift declares `.iOS(.v17)` and ships an MNISTTrainer example that trains on iOS, built through Xcode because SwiftPM cannot compile the Metal shaders. No documented M-series versus RTX 4070 benchmark exists; the mlx-benchmark tables give per-operation milliseconds for M3 Max/M4 Max (MLX and MPS) and for RTX4090/V100/A100 (CUDA) only. MuJoCo ships macOS universal binaries and `macosx_11_0_arm64` wheels for the pinned 3.3.0, renders through OpenGL 1.5 contexts (egl/glfw/osmesa), and has no official iOS build; the only Swift binding found is pinned at MuJoCo v2.3.1, "Released 3 years ago". Python 3.13 itself lists iOS as a tier-3 supported platform (PEP 730).

Whether the world processes pass torch tensors (not only numpy arrays) through multiprocessing pipes; if they do, pytorch/pytorch#153050 (open, macOS, Python 3.12+, spawn and forkserver hang at exit) applies to the release's Python 3.13 spawn context (datasource.py:495).

Whether the fp16 default precision (defaults.py:310) trains stably under MPS autocast without a GradScaler, and whether the pinned torch 2.6.0 (GradScaler .double() path, no MPSInductor) must be bumped to 2.8.0 or 2.9.0 for a Mac port (2.9.0 requires macOS 14).

MPS throughput against the README's RTX 4070 reference of 0.41 to 0.46 model steps per second with eight worlds: unmeasured; no published benchmark pairs an M-series chip with an RTX 4070, and the mlx-benchmark rows are per-operation milliseconds, not whole training steps.

Whether the Mac's unified memory suffices: the README measured about 30 GB of committed memory for the trainer and its eight world processes plus 4,287 MB of graphics memory on Windows; the MPS allocator caps a process at 1.7 x recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize (about 75% of system memory) by default.

MuJoCo on iOS: no official build exists; whether MuJoCo 3.3.0's C library compiles for arm64-apple-ios from source, and what replaces the OpenGL 1.5 eye rendering there (OpenGL ES is deprecated on iOS; MuJoCo documents no Metal renderer), is untested. The liuliu/swift-mujoco build matrix statuses for current Swift toolchains were not readable from the fetched page.

ExecuTorch on-device training on iPhone: training runs only on the portable runtime (delegates are work in progress), the exported graph must embed the loss as its first output, and the optimizers are SGD and AdamW; whether the release's 18,131,745-parameter transformer with its several losses and the planner's inner optimization export through _export_forward_backward is untested.

MLX Swift training of a model of this size on an iPhone: the only official iOS training example is a LeNet on MNIST; the iOS per-app memory ceiling for an 18M-parameter model with AdamW state and the replay memory was not researched.

Porting to MLX requires rewriting the model (encoders, forward model, wellness channels, planner, losses) in MLX's API; only the safetensors weight file transfers directly, and the parameter-name mapping between the PyTorch modules and an MLX module tree is unwritten.
The current stable ExecuTorch version number and whether the MPS backend has already been removed (scheduled for 1.4) were not verified.
The ExecuTorch and PyTorch docs sites redirected stable pages to a '2.15' path during this research; the versioned 2.9 pages were used instead, so any MPS behavior changed after 2.9.1 is not covered.
